design.data_generating_process: continuous Gaussian trait with species-specific baseline linked to geographic species centre, plus a within-species local linear effect whose sign is reversed in the specified fraction of species

comparators: naive pooled pairwise Spearman on geographic distance vs absolute trait difference
equal-species matched-null omnibus of within-species distance-trait rho
one-sided one-sample t-test on species-specific rho values
species fixed-intercept linear model with one common signed within-species slope

interpretation.supported: When all species share the same signed within-species direction, the common-slope fixed-effect model is highly powerful. When half the species reverse direction, the common signed slope cancels while the direction-invariant distance-dissimilarity matched-null statistic retains power. The key distinction is estimand alignment under directional heterogeneity, not universal superiority of one method.
not_supported: the common-slope model is generally invalid
matched-null inference is always more powerful
direction-invariant spatial organization and a common signed slope are identical estimands
all ecological traits should be analysed with absolute pairwise dissimilarity
this benchmark establishes universal type-I calibration for any method
